content: 12 Yahweh has made both ears with which to hear and eyes with which to see.

title: Proverbs 20:13
content: 13 If you sleep a lot, you will become poor; {but} if you stay awake {and work}, you will have plenty of food.

title: Proverbs 20:14
content: 14 Buyers claim that something is not good at all {when they are bargaining with the seller about its price}. But {after they buy it,} they go and boast {to their friends about the good thing that they bought}.

title: Proverbs 20:15
content: 15 Gold and precious jewels are plentiful, but the knowledgeable things that people say are rare and precious.

title: Proverbs 20:16
content: 16 Take the coats of people who promise to pay a loan for someone whom they do not know. Indeed, hold onto the coats of people who do so for a foreigner {because those people are not likely to repay those loans}.

title: Proverbs 20:17
content: 17 Food that people get by deceiving {others} may taste sweet {to them at first}, but later what they have done will be {as unpleasant to them as having} a mouth full of rocks.

title: Proverbs 20:18
content: 18 When people give you good advice, {if you do what they suggest,} your plans will succeed. Therefore, let others advise you before you start fighting a war.

title: Proverbs 20:19
content: 19 People who walk around gossiping tell {others} what is secret, so avoid people who speak carelessly.

title: Proverbs 20:20
content: 20 People who curse their parents {will die like} an oil lamp that stops burning {oil} in a totally dark place.

title: Proverbs 20:21
content: 21 If people inherit {property} hastily before the proper time, they will ultimately not receive any blessing from it.

title: Proverbs 20:22
content: 22 Do not say that you will harm someone who has harmed you. Rather, wait for Yahweh {to resolve the matter}, so that he may vindicate you.

title: Proverbs 20:23
content: 23 Yahweh detests {people dishonestly using} differing weights {to benefit themselves}. Indeed, {using} weighing instruments in order to deceive {others} is very bad.

title: Proverbs 20:24
content: 24 Yahweh directs what happens {even} to powerful people. So then, no one can comprehend what will happen to him!

title: Proverbs 20:25
content: 25 It is dangerous for people to declare thoughtlessly that they will dedicate something to Yahweh, and then later regret that they have promised to do that.

title: Proverbs 20:26
content: 26 Wise kings separate the wicked people from the good people and then punish the wicked people severely.

title: Proverbs 20:27
content: 27 Just as the light of a lamp penetrates into and illuminates a dark place, the life-breath that Yahweh puts into each person penetrates into the person’s inner being. That breath is like the presence of Yahweh, who sees everything that is inside a person.

title: Proverbs 20:28
content: 28 Being faithful and trustworthy makes kings safe. Indeed, being faithful enables them to rule securely.

title: Proverbs 20:29
content: 29 People admire young men because they are strong, but people admire old men because they have become wise.

title: Proverbs 20:30
content: 30 Flogging people for doing evil things can stop them from doing those evil things, and hitting those people {on the outside} can change who they are on the inside.

title: Proverbs 21:1
content: 1 Yahweh directs what kings think as {a farmer directs} streams of water to make them go wherever he wants {them to go}.

title: Proverbs 21:2
content: 2 People always think that what they do is right, but Yahweh {rightly} evaluates why they do those things.

title: Proverbs 21:3
content: 3 Doing what is right and fair is more acceptable to Yahweh than sacrificing {animals to him}.

title: Proverbs 21:4
content: 4 Being proud and arrogant guide what wicked people do like a lamp {shows people where to go}; they are sinful.

title: Proverbs 21:5
content: 5 What diligent people plan will certainly profit them, but all those who act too hastily will certainly become poor.

title: Proverbs 21:6
content: 6 When people gain wealth by speaking falsely, that wealth quickly vanishes like mist, {and doing that} will kill them.

title: Proverbs 21:7
content: 7 When wicked people act violently, they cause others to punish them for it because they refuse to do what is right.

title: Proverbs 21:8
content: 8 Guilty people continually do what is wrong, but innocent people do what is right.

title: Proverbs 21:9
content: 9 It is better to live {alone} in a corner of a housetop than to live inside a house with a wife who always argues {with you}.

title: Proverbs 21:10
content: 10 Wicked people strongly desire to do what is evil, they will not be merciful to the people around them.

title: Proverbs 21:11
content: 11 If you punish people who ridicule others, {then} naive people {who see you do that} will become wise, and if you teach wise people, they will become {even more} knowledgeable.

title: Proverbs 21:12
content: 12 Righteous people are able to understand what the households of wicked people do; they let the evil things that wicked people do happen to them.

title: Proverbs 21:13
content: 13 People who refuse to listen to poor people when they cry out {for help} will also cry out {for help themselves}, but no one will help them.

title: Proverbs 21:14
content: 14 Secretly giving something to an angry person will stop him from being angry. Indeed, secretly bribing a furious person will calm him down.

title: Proverbs 21:15
content: 15 Righteous people are glad when people judge justly, but judging justly terrifies people who act sinfully.

title: Proverbs 21:16
content: 16 People who stop behaving sensibly will {soon} go to the place where the spirits of dead people are.

title: Proverbs 21:17
content: 17 People who love what is pleasurable will be poor. Indeed, people who indulge themselves in wine and rich food will never be wealthy.

title: Proverbs 21:18
content: 18 Wicked people will suffer instead of righteous people, and treacherous people {will suffer} in place of upright people.

title: Proverbs 21:19
content: 19 It is better to live {alone} in a desolate land than {to live} with an argumentative and nagging wife.

title: Proverbs 21:20
content: 20 Wise people store up precious riches and olive oil, but foolish people waste everything that they have.

title: Proverbs 21:21
content: 21 People who diligently try to be righteous and faithful will live {well}, will be righteous, and people will respect them.

title: Proverbs 21:22
content: 22 Wise people know how to conquer cities that mighty warriors are defending; they can pull down the walls that people {in those cities} believe will protect them.

title: Proverbs 21:23
content: 23 People who are careful about what they say avoid becoming distressed.

title: Proverbs 21:24
content: 24 People who ridicule others are proud and arrogant; they behave furiously and presumptuously.

title: Proverbs 21:25
content: 25 Lazy people want {food}, but they will die because they refuse to work.

title: Proverbs 21:26
content: 26 Lazy people always want more things for themselves, but righteous people generously give {what they have to others}.

title: Proverbs 21:27
content: 27 {Yahweh} detests the sacrifices that wicked people offer {to him}; it is even more {detestable} when they are offering something {to Yahweh} while intending to act wickedly!

title: Proverbs 21:28
content: 28 Witnesses who lie will die, but when someone who listens carefully speaks, what he says will finish the matter.

title: Proverbs 21:29
content: 29 Wicked people pretend to know what they are doing, but upright people think about what they do.

title: Proverbs 21:30
content: 30 Even the wisest and most knowledgeable counselor is nothing compared to Yahweh.

title: Proverbs 21:31
content: 31 Soldiers prepare to fight, but Yahweh determines who wins {that fight}.

title: Proverbs 22:1
content: 1 Being someone whom people respect is more important than being very wealthy. Indeed, being someone whom others approve of is better than having silver and gold.

title: Proverbs 22:2
content: 2 Rich people and poor people have this in common: Yahweh made all of them.

title: Proverbs 22:3
content: 3 Sensible people observe something dangerous happening and avoid it, but naive people just keep going and suffer {for doing so}.

title: Proverbs 22:4
content: 4 People who are humble, who revere Yahweh, will become rich, people will respect them, and they will live {long and well}.

title: Proverbs 22:5
content: 5 Deceptive people live {dangerously,} as if they were walking down a road covered with thorns and traps, {but} people who want to stay alive avoid living that way.

title: Proverbs 22:6
content: 6 Teach children how to behave {properly}, so that when they become old, they will still continue to do so.

title: Proverbs 22:7
content: 7 Rich people reign over poor people, and people who borrow {money} from others become like slaves to the people who loaned them {money}.

title: Proverbs 22:8
content: 8 People who act unjustly will suffer for doing so, and they will no longer be able to furiously oppress other people.

title: Proverbs 22:9
content: 9 Yahweh will bless generous people because they give some of their own food to poor people.

title: Proverbs 22:10
content: 10 If you banish people who ridicule others, then people will stop arguing {with each other}, condemning {each other}, and shaming {each other}.

title: Proverbs 22:11
content: 11 People who love being sincere and speaking graciously are companions of kings.

title: Proverbs 22:12
content: 12 Yahweh preserves true sayings, but he makes what treacherous people say fail.

title: Proverbs 22:13
content: 13 Lazy people {as an excuse to not work} claim that there is a lion outside that will kill them in the street {if they go outside}.

title: Proverbs 22:14
content: 14 What adulterous women say is {as dangerous as} a deep hole {that men could fall into}; those with whom Yahweh is angry will suffer from it.

title: Proverbs 22:15
content: 15 Children naturally think foolishly, but physically disciplining them will teach them to stop being foolish.

title: Proverbs 22:16
content: 16 People who oppress poor people in order to make more money for themselves or who give things to rich people {in order to become rich} will only become poor.

title: Proverbs 22:17
content: 17 Listen carefully to what wise people have said; consider carefully what I am teaching you!

title: Proverbs 22:18
content: 18 {Do this} because if you remember these sayings and if you are always ready to repeat them {to others}, then you will be glad.

title: Proverbs 22:19
content: 19 I am teaching these sayings to you—yes, you—right now so that you will trust Yahweh.

title: Proverbs 22:20
content: 20 I am indeed writing these 30 sayings to advise and teach you.

title: Proverbs 22:21
content: 21 {I am writing them} in order to teach you what is true in trustworthy sayings, and in order to answer those who sent you with trustworthy sayings.

title: Proverbs 22:22
content: 22 Do not steal from poor people just because they are poor; and do not oppress suffering people in court.

title: Proverbs 22:23
content: 23 {Do not do these things} because Yahweh will defend those poor people when you dispute with them, and he will kill the people who stole from them.

title: Proverbs 22:24
content: 24 Do not become friends with angry people. Indeed, do not associate with people who easily become angry.

title: Proverbs 22:25
content: 25 {If you do so,} then you will act like them, and you will endanger yourself like an animal caught in a trap.

title: Proverbs 22:26
content: 26 Stay away from those people who agree to pay loans for others. {Indeed, stay away from those people} who guarantee to pay the loans of others.

title: Proverbs 22:27
content: 27 {Because} if you cannot pay back {the loan}, {then} the person to whom you owe money will surely take away even your own bed {in order to pay back the loan}.

title: Proverbs 22:28
content: 28 Do not cheat people by moving the stones that their ancestors placed long ago to mark the boundaries of their land.

title: Proverbs 22:29
content: 29 Consider this: People who work skillfully will serve kings rather than serving unknown people.

title: Proverbs 23:1
content: 1 When you sit down to eat {a meal} with someone who rules over others, pay attention to the food that is in front of you.

title: Proverbs 23:2
content: 2 Restrain yourself {from eating too much} if you like eating a lot of food.

title: Proverbs 23:3
content: 3 Do not crave the {expensive} food that the ruler has because that ruler is using that food to deceive you.

title: Proverbs 23:4
content: 4 Do not work so much that you exhaust yourself in order to become rich. Be understanding enough to stop doing so.

title: Proverbs 23:5
content: 5 As soon as you look at that wealth, it will surely be gone! {This is} because wealth certainly disappears quickly as if it had wings and flew off into the sky like a fast bird.

title: Proverbs 23:6
content: 6 Do not eat food that stingy people {give you}. Do not crave the expensive food that they have,

title: Proverbs 23:7
content: 7 because stingy people are always thinking about how much the food costs them. They will tell you to eat and drink, but they do not mean what they say.

title: Proverbs 23:8
content: 8 {When you realize this,} you will want to vomit what little food you ate. You will have wasted the kind things you said {to them}.

title: Proverbs 23:9
content: 9 Do not {try to} talk to foolish people because they will {only} despise the insightful things that you say.

title: Proverbs 23:10
content: 10 Do not cheat people by moving the old stones that mark the boundaries of their land. Do not claim the land that belongs to {defenseless} orphans,

title: Proverbs 23:11
content: 11 because {Yahweh is} the one who redeems them {and he} is powerful. He is the one who will defend them when they dispute with you.

title: Proverbs 23:12
content: 12 Consider carefully {what people say} when they correct you. Indeed, listen carefully to what people teach you.

title: Proverbs 23:13
content: 13 Do not refuse to discipline your children. If you physically punish them, they will not die.

title: Proverbs 23:14
content: 14 In fact, if you physically punish your children, you will prevent them from dying.

title: Proverbs 23:15
content: 15 My child, if you are wise, then surely I myself will be very happy,

title: Proverbs 23:16
content: 16 and I will be deeply joyful when you say what is right.

title: Proverbs 23:17
content: 17 Do not envy sinful people; instead always revere Yahweh.

title: Proverbs 23:18
content: 18 {If you do so, then} you will surely have a {good} future, and what you hope will happen will indeed occur!

title: Proverbs 23:19
content: 19 My child, listen {to me} so that you can become wise. Make yourself think about behaving rightly.

title: Proverbs 23:20
content: 20 Stay away from drunkards and gluttons,

title: Proverbs 23:21
content: 21 because drunkards and gluttons will become poor. They sleep so much that they will only have rags to wear.

title: Proverbs 23:22
content: 22 Pay attention to your father, who enabled you to exist, and continue to honor your mother when she becomes old.

title: Proverbs 23:23
content: 23 Learn what is true and remember it. Learn what is wise and instructive and what you should understand.

title: Proverbs 23:24
content: 24 Fathers of righteous people are very joyful. Indeed, those who father wise people are happy because of them.

title: Proverbs 23:25
content: 25 So do what will make your parents happy! Do what will make your mother joyful!

title: Proverbs 23:26
content: 26 My son, pay close attention to me! Carefully observe what I do!

title: Proverbs 23:27
content: 27 {Do this} because prostitutes are as dangerous as a deep hole. Indeed, {becoming involved with} an adulterous woman is as dangerous as {falling into} a well that you cannot escape from.

title: Proverbs 23:28
content: 28 These very women certainly wait {for men to seduce} like robbers {wait for people to rob}. They cause many men to become unfaithful.

title: Proverbs 23:29
content: 29 These are the kind of people who are woeful, sorrowful, and quarrelsome, who lament, get hurt for no reason, and have red eyes:

title: Proverbs 23:30
content: 30 those people who drink too much wine and are always looking around for wine {to drink} that someone has prepared.

title: Proverbs 23:31
content: 31 Do not let wine become overly attractive to you, even though it is beautifully red, glistens in the cup, and goes down your throat smoothly.

title: Proverbs 23:32
content: 32 Afterward you will feel as terrible as if a poisonous snake has bitten you.

title: Proverbs 23:33
content: 33 {When you are drunk,} you will hallucinate, and you will imagine distorted things.

title: Proverbs 23:34
content: 34 You will feel {dizzy and sick} as if you were trying to sleep on a ship that the sea was tossing back and forth. Indeed, you will feel as if you were trying to sleep while swaying at the top of a ship’s sails.

title: Proverbs 23:35
content: 35 {You will say,} “People hit me, but it did not hurt. People beat me, but I did not feel it. I wish I could be sober so that I could find even more wine {to drink} again!”

title: Proverbs 24:1
content: 1 Do not envy evil people; do not want to associate with them,

title: Proverbs 24:2
content: 2 because they plan to act violently, and they talk about doing bad things to people.

title: Proverbs 24:3
content: 3 People build households by acting wisely; they make those households stable by acting sensibly.

title: Proverbs 24:4
content: 4 By acting knowledgeably, people fill the rooms {of those households} with all kinds of valuable and delightful riches.

title: Proverbs 24:5
content: 5 Wise people are strong, and knowledgeable people make themselves more powerful,

title: Proverbs 24:6
content: 6 because letting people advise you will make you fight your war successfully, and letting many people counsel you will rescue you {from losing the war}.

title: Proverbs 24:7
content: 7 Foolish people cannot understand what is wise; they have nothing {useful} to say in court.

title: Proverbs 24:8
content: 8 {Some} people are always planning to do evil things; people refer to them as schemers.

title: Proverbs 24:9
content: 9 Foolish plans are sinful, and people detest those who ridicule others.

title: Proverbs 24:10
content: 10 If you give up during distressful times, then you are weak.

title: Proverbs 24:11
content: 11 Save people whom others are trying to kill; save the ones who will certainly die unless you do something!

title: Proverbs 24:12
content: 12 If you {falsely} claim that you did not know that those people were dying unjustly, then think about this: Yahweh knows exactly what you are thinking and he understands {what you are doing}! He is the one who keeps you alive and he knows {everything about you}! He will surely make people receive what they deserve for whatever they have done or not done!

title: Proverbs 24:13
content: 13 My child, eat honey because it tastes good, and honey dripping from the comb tastes sweet.

title: Proverbs 24:14
content: 14 Be aware that what is wise is like honey for you. If you become wise, then you will have a {good} future, and what you hope will happen will indeed occur!

title: Proverbs 24:15
content: 15 Do not be like wicked people and hide in wait in order to attack the places where righteous people dwell. Do not devastate the places where righteous people rest!

title: Proverbs 24:16
content: 16 {Do not do so} because righteous people can recover many times when disastrous things happen to them, but disastrous things will destroy wicked people.

title: Proverbs 24:17
content: 17 Do not be happy when something disastrous happens to your adversaries. Indeed, do not rejoice when that happens!

title: Proverbs 24:18
content: 18 If you do, then Yahweh will notice and disapprove, so that he stops being angry with your enemies.

title: Proverbs 24:19
content: 19 Do not worry about people who do what is evil. Do not be envious of wicked people.

title: Proverbs 24:20
content: 20 {Do not do so} because evil people will not have {good} futures, {but} wicked people {will merely die} like an oil lamp that stops burning {oil}.

title: Proverbs 24:21
content: 21 My child, reverently fear Yahweh and kings. Avoid people who rebel {against either Yahweh or the king},

title: Proverbs 24:22
content: 22 because disastrous things will happen quickly to those people, and no one knows how terribly both Yahweh and kings can destroy {others}!

title: Proverbs 24:23
content: 23 Here are more things that wise people have said: It is very evil to favor someone when you judge.

title: Proverbs 24:24
content: 24 If anyone declares that a guilty person is innocent, many people will curse him and whole people groups will hate him.

title: Proverbs 24:25
content: 25 However, people who condemn {guilty people} will prosper, and Yahweh will bless them well.

title: Proverbs 24:26
content: 26 People who answer honestly show that they are true friends.

title: Proverbs 24:27
content: 27 Do the work you must do outside and prepare your fields before you build your house.

title: Proverbs 24:28
content: 28 Do not testify against someone if you do not have a good reason {to do so}, and do not try to deceive people by what you say.

title: Proverbs 24:29
content: 29 Do not say, “I will do to him that same {bad} thing that he did to me; I will pay him back for what he did to me!”

title: Proverbs 24:30
content: 30 I walked by the land of a lazy person and past the vineyard of someone who does not think wisely.

title: Proverbs 24:31
content: 31 And I saw that thistles and weeds were everywhere in that field and vineyard. Even the stone wall surrounding them had fallen down.

title: Proverbs 24:32
content: 32 When I saw {that}, I considered carefully {what I was seeing}. When I observed {that}, I learned {this}:

title: Proverbs 24:33
content: 33 {If you say to yourself,} “Let me sleep just a little more! Let me lay my hands {across my chest} in order to rest comfortably for a little while longer!”

title: Proverbs 24:34
content: 34 Then {the result of being so lazy will be that} you will become poor and needy just as surely as if a thief has robbed you.

title: Proverbs 25:1
content: 1 Here are more wise sayings said by Solomon that the scribes who served Hezekiah, the king of Judah, copied {from a scroll that Solomon had written}:

title: Proverbs 25:2
content: 2 God shows how glorious he is when he makes something that is difficult for people to understand. But kings show how glorious they are when they explain something {that is difficult for people to understand}.

title: Proverbs 25:3
content: 3 As people cannot fully understand how high the sky is or how deep the earth is, so they cannot fully understand what kings think.

title: Proverbs 25:4
content: 4 People who make things from metal must remove impurities from silver before they can make {that silver into} something useful.

title: Proverbs 25:5
content: 5 {In the same way,} people must remove wicked advisers from the presence of kings so that they can rule securely by being righteous.

title: Proverbs 25:6
content: 6 Do not promote yourself in front of kings, and do not pretend to be great.

title: Proverbs 25:7
content: 7 {Do not do so} because it is better if someone invites you to sit in a place that is closer {to the king}, than for someone to embarrass you in front of a royal official whom you have seen {by telling you to sit farther away from the king}.

title: Proverbs 25:8
content: 8 Do not plead your case too quickly against someone you know. If you do, then you will not know what to do when that person {wins the case and} embarrasses you!

title: Proverbs 25:9
content: 9 If you do indeed plead your case against someone you know, {settle it between yourselves and} do not tell {others} any secret about that person.

title: Proverbs 25:10
content: 10 If you do {tell a secret}, then the people who hear you may shame you {for it}, and people will speak badly about you from then on.

title: Proverbs 25:11
content: 11 When someone says something that is very appropriate to a situation, it is {as delightful as seeing} golden apples in a setting of silver.

title: Proverbs 25:12
content: 12 When a wise person rebukes someone who is willing to listen, it is {as valuable as} a gold ring or jewelry made from the best gold.

title: Proverbs 25:13
content: 13 Reliable messengers are {as refreshing} to those who send them as cold snow would be {refreshing} during the {summer} harvest time; they refresh the people whom they serve.

title: Proverbs 25:14
content: 14 People who brag about giving something but then do not give it are as disappointing as clouds and wind that do not bring rain.

title: Proverbs 25:15
content: 15 People can persuade leaders by being patient, and by speaking gently people can convince those who oppose them {to agree with them}.

title: Proverbs 25:16
content: 16 If you discover some wild honey, do not eat too much of it. If you do, then you will become sick from it and vomit.

title: Proverbs 25:17
content: 17 {In the same way,} do not visit too often the houses of your friends. If you do, then they may feel that they have had too much of you and {even} hate you.

title: Proverbs 25:18
content: 18 People who lie when they testify against other people are {deadly, as if they had attacked them with} a club, a sword, or a piercing arrow.

title: Proverbs 25:19
content: 19 Trusting treacherous people during distressful times is {like trying to eat with} a rotten tooth or {trying to walk with} a crippled foot.

title: Proverbs 25:20
content: 20 Singing songs to someone who is sad is {as unhelpful as} taking a coat off of someone in cold weather or pouring vinegar on soda.

title: Proverbs 25:21
content: 21 Feed your enemies if they are hungry; give them something to drink if they are thirsty.

title: Proverbs 25:22
content: 22 {Do so} because by doing so you {will shame them, as if you} were pouring burning coals on top of them, and Yahweh will reward you {for doing so}.

title: Proverbs 25:23
content: 23 When wind blows from the north, that produces rain. {Similarly,} when people tell the secrets {of others}, {that produces} angry people.

title: Proverbs 25:24
content: 24 It is better to live {alone} in a corner of a housetop than to live inside a house with a wife who always argues {with you}.

title: Proverbs 25:25
content: 25 When people hear something good from a faraway place, it is as {refreshing as drinking} cold water when one is thirsty.

title: Proverbs 25:26
content: 26 When righteous people yield to wicked people, it is {as bad as} a spring that people have made murky by walking in it or {as bad as} a polluted fountain.

title: Proverbs 25:27
content: 27 {As} it is not good to eat too much honey; {so it is not} honorable to try to make people honor you.

title: Proverbs 25:28
content: 28 People who cannot control themselves are {as defenseless as} a city that an army has broken into and knocked down its walls.

title: Proverbs 26:1
content: 1 Honoring foolish people is just as inappropriate as snow {falling} in {hot} summer and rain {falling} during the time to harvest crops.

title: Proverbs 26:2
content: 2 Just as a bird will fly by {and not land on you}, so a curse will not harm you if you are innocent.

title: Proverbs 26:3
content: 3 As people must whip horses and bridle donkeys {in order to guide them}, so people must physically punish foolish people {in order to guide them}.

title: Proverbs 26:4
content: 4 Do not reply to foolish people according to their foolish way of thinking. If you do, then you also will be foolish.

title: Proverbs 26:5
content: 5 Reply to foolish people according to their foolish way of thinking. If you do not, then they may think that they are wise.

title: Proverbs 26:6
content: 6 Anyone who asks a foolish person to take a message to someone is {doing something as foolish as} cutting off his own feet or drinking poison.

title: Proverbs 26:7
content: 7 {As} the legs of people who cannot walk are useless, so are the sayings that foolish people say.

title: Proverbs 26:8
content: 8 Honoring foolish people is just {as useless} as a harmless weapon.

title: Proverbs 26:9
content: 9 A drunken person picks up a thorn {and it will hurt someone}, {in the same way} a foolish person says a proverb {that can only be harmful}.

title: Proverbs 26:10
content: 10 People who employ foolish people or random strangers are {as dangerous} as someone who randomly shoots arrows at people.

title: Proverbs 26:11
content: 11 Foolish people who do the same foolish thing over and over again are like dogs that eat what they have vomited up.

title: Proverbs 26:12
content: 12 Consider this: Foolish people are more likely to learn than people who {wrongly} think that they are {already} wise.

title: Proverbs 26:13
content: 13 Lazy people claim that there is a lion in the path or in the midst of the streets {so that they can stay inside their houses and do nothing}.

title: Proverbs 26:14
content: 14 As doors swing on their hinges {and do not go anywhere}, so lazy people turn back and forth in their beds.

title: Proverbs 26:15
content: 15 Lazy people put their hands in a dish {of food}, {but} they are so lazy that they will not lift the food to their mouths.

title: Proverbs 26:16
content: 16 A {typical} lazy person {wrongly} thinks that he is wiser than several people who answer intelligently.

title: Proverbs 26:17
content: 17 People who make themselves angry because of an argument that does not concern them are {as foolish as} people who grab the ears of a dog that is passing by.

title: Proverbs 26:18-19
content: 18-19 People who trick others and then say that they were just joking are {as dangerous} as a crazy person who shoots deadly flaming arrows {at people}.

title: Proverbs 26:20
content: 20 Fires stop burning when they have nothing {to burn}. In the same way, people stop arguing when no one is gossiping.

title: Proverbs 26:21
content: 21 {As} charcoal keeps coals burning and wood keeps fires burning, so people who always argue keep other people arguing.

title: Proverbs 26:22
content: 22 People are eager to listen to what people who gossip say, and what they say deeply affects those who hear it.

title: Proverbs 26:23
content: 23 People who fervently say {that they are your friend} while thinking about doing evil things {to you} {are as deceptive as} a {cheap} clay pot that someone has made to look like silver.

title: Proverbs 26:24
content: 24 People who hate you will use what they say to hide what they feel, but they are {really} thinking about how to betray you.

title: Proverbs 26:25
content: 25 Do not believe those people when they speak kindly to you, because they are thinking many detestable things.

title: Proverbs 26:26
content: 26 Although those people deceive others by pretending that they do not hate you, When people gather together, they will discover how wicked those people are.

title: Proverbs 26:27
content: 27 People who dig pits to trap others will fall into those pits instead; and people who try to crush others with stones will become crushed by those stones instead.

title: Proverbs 26:28
content: 28 Liars hate the people whom they hurt, and flatterers cause disastrous things to happen.

title: Proverbs 27:1
content: 1 Do not brag about {what you will do} tomorrow, because you do not know what will happen then.

title: Proverbs 27:2
content: 2 Do not praise yourself; let someone else praise you. Indeed, let other people praise you, not yourself.

title: Proverbs 27:3
content: 3 Stones and sand are heavy, but fools are so annoying that they are harder to bear than either of those.

title: Proverbs 27:4
content: 4 Angry people are cruel and furious people are destructive, but no one can withstand jealous people!

title: Proverbs 27:5
content: 5 It is better to correct people openly, than to love them without showing them that you love them.

title: Proverbs 27:6
content: 6 Friends will be faithful to you by criticizing you {when necessary}, but enemies will deceive you by acting affectionately toward you.

title: Proverbs 27:7
content: 7 When people have full stomachs, they do not want to eat {even} honey. But when people are hungry, {even} bitter things taste sweet to them.

title: Proverbs 27:8
content: 8 People who stray from their homes are like birds that stray from their nests.

title: Proverbs 27:9
content: 9 Fragrant oil and perfume make people feel happy, but having a friend who advises you sincerely is even better.

title: Proverbs 27:10
content: 10 Do not ignore your friends or your father’s friends. Do not {think that you must} go to the house of a relative when something disastrous happens to you. {Rather,} it is better to go to a nearby neighbor than to relatives who live far away.

title: Proverbs 27:11
content: 11 My child, make me happy by becoming wise. Then I will be able to reply to anyone who argues against me.

title: Proverbs 27:12
content: 12 Sensible people observe something dangerous happening and avoid it, but naive people {ignorantly} do not avoid it and suffer {for doing so}.

title: Proverbs 27:13
content: 13 Take the coats of people who promise to pay a loan for someone whom they do not know. Indeed, hold onto the coats of people who do so for a foreigner.

title: Proverbs 27:14
content: 14 If you rise early in the morning and loudly call out a blessing to your neighbor {while he is still sleeping}, he will consider it to be a curse{, not a blessing}.

title: Proverbs 27:15
content: 15 A wife who always argues {with you} is as {annoying as} constantly dripping water on a rainy day.

title: Proverbs 27:16
content: 16 It is as difficult to stop her {from arguing} as stopping the wind, or catching oil in one hand.

title: Proverbs 27:17
content: 17 {We can use} one iron tool to sharpen another iron tool; {similarly,} when one person shares what he is thinking, it can help another person to think more clearly.

title: Proverbs 27:18
content: 18 Just as people who take care of fruit trees will also eat the fruit from those trees, so too will masters honor their servants who guard them.

title: Proverbs 27:19
content: 19 When people look in water, the water reflects their faces. In the same way, what people think reveals what kinds of people they are.

title: Proverbs 27:20
content: 20 Just as the place where dead people go never becomes full; so people never stop wanting {things}.

title: Proverbs 27:21
content: 21 People use crucibles and furnaces to test and refine silver and gold. In the same way, people can know what kind of person someone is {by how he reacts} when people praise him.

title: Proverbs 27:22
content: 22 If you were to crush a fool the way that you would crush grain {into powder}, you would still not be able to find any part of him that is not foolish.

title: Proverbs 27:23
content: 23 Be fully aware of how your sheep are doing. Indeed, consider carefully how your animals fare.

title: Proverbs 27:24
content: 24 {Do so} because riches will not last forever. Even a king’s family will not rule forever!

title: Proverbs 27:25
content: 25 Harvest the grass and then you will see new grass. Collect {and store} the plants that grow on the hillside.

title: Proverbs 27:26
content: 26 {If you do these things, then} you will have lambs with wool that you can clothe yourself with. You will also have male goats that you can sell for enough money to buy a field.

title: Proverbs 27:27
content: 27 You will even have female goats that produce enough milk for yourself, your family, and your servant girls to drink.

title: Proverbs 28:1
content: 1 Wicked people run away even though no one is chasing them, but righteous people are as brave as lions.

title: Proverbs 28:2
content: 2 When the people in a country sin, they will continually have {new} leaders; but when they have a truly knowledgeable ruler, then they will have a {stable} government that will last.

title: Proverbs 28:3
content: 3 A poor person who oppresses other poor people is {as destructive as} rain that washes away {the crops}, leaving nothing to eat.

title: Proverbs 28:4
content: 4 People who reject {Yahweh’s} laws say good things about wicked people; but people who obey those laws oppose such wicked people.

title: Proverbs 28:5
content: 5 Evil people cannot comprehend what is just, but people who desire to please Yahweh comprehend everything {about it}.

title: Proverbs 28:6
content: 6 It is better to be poor and honest than to be dishonest and rich.

title: Proverbs 28:7
content: 7 Young people who obey {Yahweh’s} laws are wise, but young people who carouse with gluttons disgrace their fathers.

title: Proverbs 28:8
content: 8 Money that people gain by charging an unreasonably large amount of interest {from those to whom they loan money} will {eventually} belong to someone who is kind to poor people.

title: Proverbs 28:9
content: 9 Yahweh detests hearing prayers from people who refuse to obey his laws.

title: Proverbs 28:10
content: 10 People who guide upright people to act evilly will destroy themselves by what they do, but people whom Yahweh does not blame {for acting wickedly} will receive what is good.

title: Proverbs 28:11
content: 11 Rich people tend to think that they are wise, but perceptive poor people can tell whether or not this is true.

title: Proverbs 28:12
content: 12 People celebrate when righteous people become powerful, but people hide when wicked people become powerful.

title: Proverbs 28:13
content: 13 People who {try to} hide the sinful things that they do will never be successful, but Yahweh will be merciful to people who confess the sinful things that they have done and stop doing them.

title: Proverbs 28:14
content: 14 People who constantly examine how they are thinking and behaving are happy, but bad things will happen to people who become uncaring about those things.

title: Proverbs 28:15
content: 15 Wicked people who rule over poor people are {as dangerous as} a roaring lion or attacking bear.

title: Proverbs 28:16
content: 16 Leaders who are not sensible severely oppress {other people}, {but} people who despise gaining wealth unjustly will live for a long time.

title: Proverbs 28:17
content: 17 People who murder others will keep running away {from those who would punish them} until they die. Do not help them!

title: Proverbs 28:18
content: 18 Yahweh will rescue people who continually do what is right, but people who behave dishonestly will ruin themselves in the end.

title: Proverbs 28:19
content: 19 People who work hard will have enough food {to eat}, but people who waste time doing worthless things will only be poor.

title: Proverbs 28:20
content: 20 Yahweh abundantly blesses faithful people, but he will certainly punish people who are eager to be wealthy.

title: Proverbs 28:21
content: 21 Although it is very evil to unfairly favor one person over another, some people will sin {by doing so} to get even a small bribe.

title: Proverbs 28:22
content: 22 People who are eager to become rich are greedy. They do not realize that they will become poor.

title: Proverbs 28:23
content: 23 Afterward, people appreciate someone who has corrected them more than {they appreciate} someone who has spoken flatteringly {to them}.

title: Proverbs 28:24
content: 24 People who rob their parents and say that doing so is not wrong are as bad as thieves.

title: Proverbs 28:25
content: 25 Greedy people cause people to argue with each other, but Yahweh will prosper people who trust him.

title: Proverbs 28:26
content: 26 People who trust in themselves are foolish, but people who act wisely are the ones who will escape {what is dangerous}.

title: Proverbs 28:27
content: 27 People who give poor people {what they need} will have all that they need, but there are many who will curse people who ignore poor people.

title: Proverbs 28:28
content: 28 People hide when wicked people become powerful, but when those wicked people die, there will be more and more righteous people.

title: Proverbs 29:1
content: 1 Some people remain stubborn even though other people often correct them; but someday something will destroy them quickly, and they will not be able to recover.

title: Proverbs 29:2
content: 2 People are joyful when righteous people become influential, but people are miserable when wicked people rule {over them}.

title: Proverbs 29:3
content: 3 People who cherish what is wise make their fathers happy, but people who have sex with prostitutes waste all their money.

title: Proverbs 29:4
content: 4 Kings make the people in their land succeed by acting justly, but leaders who take money dishonestly ruin the people in their land.

title: Proverbs 29:5
content: 5 People who flatter others are really just preparing to exploit them in some way

title: Proverbs 29:6
content: 6 Evil people endanger themselves by acting sinfully, but righteous people sing joyfully and are happy.

title: Proverbs 29:7
content: 7 Righteous people know that they should treat poor people justly, but wicked people do not {even} understand that they should know {this}.

title: Proverbs 29:8
content: 8 People who mock others agitate people throughout a city, but wise people enable others to remain calm.

title: Proverbs 29:9
content: 9 If wise people dispute with foolish people, the foolish people will become angry and sneer and not resolve anything.

title: Proverbs 29:10
content: 10 Murderers despise people who always try to do what is right, but righteous people try to protect them.

title: Proverbs 29:11
content: 11 Foolish people uncontrollably express everything that they feel, but wise people control how they express what they feel.

title: Proverbs 29:12
content: 12 Leaders who believe the false things that people tell them have only wicked servants.

title: Proverbs 29:13
content: 13 Poor people and the people who oppress {them} have {at least} one thing in common: Yahweh is the one who causes both of them to live.

title: Proverbs 29:14
content: 14 Kings who judge poor people according to what is true will always rule securely.

title: Proverbs 29:15
content: 15 If parents punish and correct their children, doing so can make those children wise; but if parents let their children do whatever they want to do, then their children will disgrace them.

title: Proverbs 29:16
content: 16 People sin more when wicked people rule over them, but {someday} Yahweh will destroy those wicked people, and righteous people will see it happen.

title: Proverbs 29:17
content: 17 If you discipline your children, then you will no longer feel worried {about their behavior} and they will make you very happy.

title: Proverbs 29:18
content: 18 When the people {of a nation} do not have messages from Yahweh {through his prophets}, then they do not control themselves, but people who obey {Yahweh’s} laws are happy.

title: Proverbs 29:19
content: 19 You cannot correct servants by {only} speaking to them because they will not do what you say even though they understand {what you say}.

title: Proverbs 29:20
content: 20 Consider this: Foolish people are more likely to do well in life than people who speak thoughtlessly.

title: Proverbs 29:21
content: 21 If you give your servants everything they want when they are young, then they will eventually be arrogant.

title: Proverbs 29:22
content: 22 People who easily become angry cause people to argue. Indeed, angry people cause many people to sin.

title: Proverbs 29:23
content: 23 People will humiliate proud people for being proud, but people will honor those who are humble.

title: Proverbs 29:24
content: 24 People who take a share of a thief’s spoils greatly endanger themselves; They hear that Yahweh will curse them {for not testifying to what they know}, but they do not say anything {about the crime}.

title: Proverbs 29:25
content: 25 Being anxious is {as dangerous as walking into} a trap, but Yahweh will protect people who trust in him.

title: Proverbs 29:26
content: 26 Many {people} want leaders to help them, but Yahweh is the {only} one who {surely} does for them what is just.

title: Proverbs 29:27
content: 27 Righteous people detest unjust people, and wicked people detest people who do the right thing.

title: Proverbs 30:1
content: 1 {These are} the sayings of Agur son of Jakeh, which Yahweh told him to say; {these are what} Agur declared to both Ithiel and Ucal:

title: Proverbs 30:2
content: 2 I am certainly less intelligent than other people. Indeed, I do not understand as much as everyone else understands!

title: Proverbs 30:3
content: 3 I have not learned how to become wise, nor do I know {much} about {Yahweh,} the Holy One.

title: Proverbs 30:4
content: 4 {But I will say this:} Surely nobody has ever gone to heaven and returned to earth! Surely nobody has ever controlled the wind! Surely nobody has ever gathered the water for rain in the clouds! Surely nobody has ever formed the boundaries of the earth! You do not know the name of any such person, or the name of his son. Therefore, you {also} do not know {much}!

title: Proverbs 30:5
content: 5 Everything that God says is true; he is {like} a shield that protects people who trust him to protect them.

title: Proverbs 30:6
content: 6 Never claim that God has said something other than what he has {actually} said. If you do that, then he will correct you and he will prove that you lied {about what he said}.

title: Proverbs 30:7
content: 7 {God,} I ask you to do two things; please do them for me before I die:

title: Proverbs 30:8
content: 8 {Please} prevent me from being dishonest or speaking what is not true. {Please} do not let me become too poor or too rich, {but} just provide the proper amount of food for me.

title: Proverbs 30:9
content: 9 Because if I become rich, I might say that I do not know you and that I do not need you; and if I become poor, I might dishonor you by stealing things.

title: Proverbs 30:10
content: 10 Never say bad things about servants to the people whom they serve. If you do, then they will curse you, and people will hold you responsible {for what you said}.

title: Proverbs 30:11
content: 11 Some people disrespect their parents.

title: Proverbs 30:12
content: 12 Some people think that they are sinless, but they have committed disgusting sins, {like} people who have covered themselves with excrement.

title: Proverbs 30:13
content: 13 Some people are very proud! They think that they are better than other people.

title: Proverbs 30:14
content: 14 Some people are very cruel toward others; they harshly oppress and destroy poor people as fierce animals attack and eat other animals.

title: Proverbs 30:15
content: 15 {Greedy people are like} the offspring of leeches {because they} always want other people to give them more. There are three, even four things that always want more:

title: Proverbs 30:16
content: 16 the place where dead people are, childless women, soil that never receives enough water, and fire that keeps consuming more.

title: Proverbs 30:17
content: 17 People who ridicule their fathers, and refuse to obey their mothers deserve to {die and} have wild animals eat their {dead} bodies.

title: Proverbs 30:18
content: 18 There are three, even four things, that are too amazing for me to comprehend:

title: Proverbs 30:19
content: 19 how a bird flies in the air, how a snake slithers over a rock, how a ship sails in the middle of the ocean, and how a young man loves a young woman.

title: Proverbs 30:20
content: 20 Acting adulterously is {as easy} for adulterous women as eating and wiping their mouths. Afterward, they claim that they have not sinned at all.

title: Proverbs 30:21
content: 21 There are three, even four, things that {the people in} the world cannot tolerate:

title: Proverbs 30:22
content: 22 what slaves do who become rulers, what worthless people do when they have plenty of food to eat,

title: Proverbs 30:23
content: 23 what women whom people hate do when they marry someone, and what servant girls do who replace the wives of their masters.

title: Proverbs 30:24
content: 24 There are four creatures in the world that are small but extremely wise:

title: Proverbs 30:25
content: 25 Although ants are not strong, they store up their food during the summer {so that they have it to eat during the winter}.

title: Proverbs 30:26
content: 26 Although hyraxes are {also} not strong, they are able to make their homes {high up in the rocks} on cliffs.

title: Proverbs 30:27
content: 27 Although locusts do not have a king, they move in orderly groups like soldiers in an army.

title: Proverbs 30:28
content: 28 Although anyone can {easily} catch lizards in his hands, they can freely enter into kings’ palaces.

title: Proverbs 30:29
content: 29 There are three, even four, things that look very impressive when they walk:

title: Proverbs 30:30
content: 30 lions, which are the most powerful animals and never flee from anything,

title: Proverbs 30:31
content: 31 strutting male birds, male goats, and kings whom people are afraid to rebel against.

title: Proverbs 30:32
content: 32 If you have acted foolishly by bragging about yourself, or if you were plotting {to do what is evil}, then stop doing so immediately!

title: Proverbs 30:33
content: 33 {Stop doing so} because just as churning milk produces butter, and squeezing a nose produces blood, making people angry causes them to fight.

title: Proverbs 31:1
content: 1 {These are} the sayings of King Lemuel; Yahweh had spoken these sayings that his mother had taught him:

title: Proverbs 31:2
content: 2 My son, whom I gave birth to and whom I vowed {to dedicate to Yahweh}, listen to me!

title: Proverbs 31:3
content: 3 Do not exhaust yourself by having sex with women; they can destroy kings.

title: Proverbs 31:4
content: 4 Lemuel, kings and dignitaries should not {constantly} drink wine, or {greatly} desire to drink what can intoxicate {them}.

title: Proverbs 31:5
content: 5 {They must not do this} so that they do not forget the laws {that they have made} and prevent all suffering people from getting what they legally deserve.

title: Proverbs 31:6
content: 6 Let dying people drink what can intoxicate {them}, and let miserable people drink wine.

title: Proverbs 31:7
content: 7 They can drink {what can intoxicate them} to forget that they are poor and to completely forget what troubles them.

title: Proverbs 31:8
content: 8 Defend those who cannot speak {for themselves}; {defend} all those whom others are threatening to kill so that they get what they legally deserve.

title: Proverbs 31:9
content: 9 Defend, judge rightly, and plead for suffering and poor people to get what they legally deserve.

title: Proverbs 31:10
content: 10 Virtuous and capable women are difficult to find! This kind of woman is more valuable than precious jewels.

title: Proverbs 31:11
content: 11 Her husband completely trusts her, and he will always gain many things {because of her}.

title: Proverbs 31:12
content: 12 Such a woman benefits her husband for as long as she lives.

title: Proverbs 31:13
content: 13 She gets materials to make clothing for both warm and cool weather, and she enjoys making that clothing.

title: Proverbs 31:14
content: 14 She is like merchant ships because she brings food to her home from distant places.

title: Proverbs 31:15
content: 15 She gets up before dawn in order to prepare food for her family and to prepare some {food} for her female servants.

title: Proverbs 31:16
content: 16 She carefully evaluates a field and then buys it. {Then} she uses some of what she earned by working to plant a vineyard {in it}.

title: Proverbs 31:17
content: 17 She keeps her body strong, and she makes her arms strong {by working hard}.

title: Proverbs 31:18
content: 18 She knows that what she does is very profitable. She works late into the night.

title: Proverbs 31:19
content: 19 She makes thread {for clothing} with her own hands.

title: Proverbs 31:20
content: 20 She generously helps people who are poor and suffering.

title: Proverbs 31:21
content: 21 She is not worried that her family will be cold during cold weather because her whole family has the best clothing.

title: Proverbs 31:22
content: 22 She makes her own blankets to cover beds. She wears clothing made from expensive cloth.

title: Proverbs 31:23
content: 23 People respect such a woman’s husband at the {city} gates, when he sits {there} with the {other} leaders of the city.

title: Proverbs 31:24
content: 24 This woman makes clothing and sells it. She also sells belts to merchants.

title: Proverbs 31:25
content: 25 People notice how strong and dignified she is, and she is cheerful about what will happen in the future.

title: Proverbs 31:26
content: 26 She speaks wisely, and when she speaks, she teaches {others} to be faithful and kind.

title: Proverbs 31:27
content: 27 She carefully watches what happens in her household, and she is never lazy.

title: Proverbs 31:28
content: 28 This woman’s children stand respectfully and declare that she lives well. Her husband says good things about her, as well.

title: Proverbs 31:29
content: 29 He says to her, “Many women have acted virtuously and capably, but you indeed have done better than them all!”

title: Proverbs 31:30
content: 30 Charming women {who are not good} can deceive people into thinking that they are good, and beautiful women will be beautiful for only a short time. However, people will {always} praise those women who reverently fear Yahweh.

title: Proverbs 31:31
content: 31 Give to such women what they have earned, and praise them publicly for what they have done.
